result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the CSS is already responsive, explain why its pieces work, and add no breakpoints. Both go against the rubric by giving a list of four fixes and a full rewritten stylesheet, where one or two optional notes were wanted. A is a little shorter and keeps closer to the original, while B adds an unrelated `img { display: block }` change and a long reasoning section that makes it even longer. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that the CSS is already responsive, add no media queries, and explain why the existing pieces work. Both also undercut that verdict by listing four fixes and returning a full revised stylesheet. A keeps the original compact form and gives a slightly clearer account of the clamp limits, capped measure and query-free grid, while B reformats the whole file into a longer layout and adds more caveats and a breakpoint-testing offer, which makes it longer and less in line with the rubric.
